Who we are 

We simplify wealth creation. Founded in 2014 in Vienna, Austria by Eric Demuth, Paul Klanschek and Christian Trummer, we’re here to help people trust themselves enough to build their financial freedom — for now and the future. Our user-friendly, trade-everything platform empowers both first-time investors and seasoned experts to invest in the cryptocurrencies, crypto indices, stocks*, precious metals and commodities* they want — with any sized budget, 24/7. Our global team works across different cultures and time zones, bringing our products to more than 7 million customers, making us one of Europe’s safest and most secure platforms that powers modern investing.

Headquartered in Austria but operating across Europe, our products are built by fast-moving, talented, “roll-up-your-sleeves-and-make-it-happen” kind of people. It’s these diverse perspectives and innovative minds operating as ONE TEAM that keep Bitpanda at the cutting edge of our industry. So if you’re someone who thinks big, moves fast and wants to make an impact right from day one, then get ready to join our industry-changing team. Let’s go!

Your mission 

As an Information Security Senior Associate, you will execute and mature key parts of our GRC program in a regulated fintech environment. You’ll take charge of specific GRC domains (e.g., ISMS/ISO 27001, audit, risk management, TPRM), driving control design, testing, and cross-functional coordination. Operating with strong autonomy, you'll bridge high-level strategy and daily operations to help scale our security governance.

What you’ll do

  • GRC domain execution: Manage daily operations of assigned GRC domains, track yearly plans, and build scalable playbooks to reduce audit friction and improve control consistency.
  • Assurance & audits: Coordinate internal and external audits end-to-end (planning, evidence gathering, auditor Q&A, remediation). Translate regulatory requirements into actionable plans and draft formal audit responses.
  • Risk management: Facilitate risk assessments for systems and products. Drive treatment plans with owners, escalate unacceptable residual risks, and prepare clear KRI/KPI reporting for leadership.
  • Third-party risk management (if in scope): Drive vendor due diligence by evaluating security evidence and tracking remediation. Partner with Legal and Procurement to embed security obligations into contracts.
  • Control testing & improvement: Execute risk-based control testing (design and operating effectiveness). Identify recurring failures, propose process upgrades, and implement dashboards for evidence collection.

Who you are

  • 2–4 years of experience in GRC, audit, security risk management, or compliance.
  • Strong knowledge of ISO 27001 (or similar frameworks) and the ability to map requirements to real operational processes.
  • Hands-on experience coordinating audits or risk assessments from planning through closure.
  • Solid grasp of security fundamentals (IAM, SDLC, incident and vulnerability management, logging/monitoring, third-party risk).
  • Excellent communication skills: can independently produce clear policy documentation, audit narratives, and manage stakeholder relationships.

What’s in it for you

  • Flexibility to work where you thrive – Enjoy the freedom of our Hybrid working model, combining onsite collaboration and remote work, with an additional 25 days per year to work from a city or country of your choice.
  • Reward for your impact – Receive a competitive total compensation package aligned with Bitpanda’s pay-for-impact policy, including participation in our stock option plan.
  • Support for your mental wellbeing – Access confidential coaching, counselling, and mental health resources whenever you need them through OpenUP.
  • Time to recharge – On top of your standard annual leave, prioritise your wellbeing in 2027 with 3 additional days of paid time off to rest, reset, and recharge, available once you’ve been with us for 6 months.
  • Continuous learning and growth – Grow your skills and stay ahead in your career with unlimited access to Udemy’s library of online courses at your own pace.
  • Exclusive perks and rewards – Enjoy discounts, rewards, and perks from partners worldwide across lifestyle, wellness, tech, and travel.
  • Support during life milestones – Take advantage of up to 8 additional weeks of gender-neutral new parent leave to welcome and bond with your new addition to the family.
  • Fuel and focus on-site – Pandas in Vienna, Bucharest, Barcelona, and Berlin can enjoy free onsite dining, with freshly prepared lunches and snacks to keep you fueled and focused all day long.
  • Recognition for your contributions – Celebrate milestones and achievements with recognition and rewards for your Tenure at Bitpanda.
  • Show your Bitpanda pride – Access exclusive Bitpanda-branded merchandise and gear to represent.
  • Connect and celebrate with your team – Join unforgettable company events, from our Winter Party in Vienna to gatherings worldwide, fostering fun, connection, and celebration

       .…and even more location-specific benefits designed to make life at Bitpanda even more rewarding wherever you are.

Above all, you will have the opportunity to learn and grow as part of Bitpanda’s incredible journey towards being Europe’s future #1 investment platform.

Bitpanda is committed to fostering a fair and equal environment based on trust and mutual respect. We believe that a diverse and inclusive workplace is paramount to our success and we are committed to building a team that represents a wide variety of backgrounds, perspectives, and skills.
* These benefits may be adjusted at Bitpanda’s discretion and do not apply to our internships and exceptions to our Hybrid Working policy apply to teams with shift schedules or for folks whose roles require them to be in-office (think: Workplaces team or IT).

About Ramp

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

About the Role

As a member of Ramp's Risk Strategy & Operations, you will drive operational initiatives related to underwriting, customer risk management, and fraud. This role requires an understanding of underwriting processes, fluency with data, and the ability to analyze risk vectors such as credit and fraud risks. We take our responsibility to serve our customers’ commitment to their financial health seriously, and our approach is anchored in data-driven and systematic decisions to delight our customers.

Please note: This role follows a Sunday–Thursday workweek.

 

What You'll Do

  • Have the ability to grow, develop and learn in a fast-paced, start-up environment

Overview

CoinTracker is on a mission to unlock everyone's financial potential so they can build the life they want. We started with crypto, building the tax and portfolio tools that millions of users trust to trade digital assets with peace of mind. Nino builds the next layer of financial fluency for our users. Nino is an AI-powered financial operating system that makes comprehensive, expert-level tax and financial planning advice accessible.

More on Nino: Comprehensive tax and financial planning strategies are currently locked behind high AUM fees or require enough wealth to have a family office. We are turning expert judgment into software so we can serve millions. AI is going to redefine how people understand their finances and how tax advice gets delivered. Not in ten years, in 2026. You can help define that, or spend the next few years adapting to rules someone else wrote. Nino sits inside CoinTracker ($100M raised, partnered with Coinbase, TurboTax, H&R Block, and Thomson Reuters) with the autonomy of an early-stage startup and the reach of an established platform.

 

Your mission

As Product Engineer, you'll own customer problems from the first conversation to a working product. You'll talk to users, shape the idea, design the experience, and build it across the stack. You'll work closely with engineers, design, and our CPAs and Financial Planners to turn complicated financial work into software people can understand and trust.

Your one-year outcomes

  • Customers rely on what you build. You've shipped meaningful features end to end, with evidence that customers use them and find them valuable.

  • More financial work gets done. Workflows you own help households and advisors complete tasks with less manual effort, fewer handoffs, and clearer next steps.

  • The experience holds up. Your features are easy to use and reliable in practice, including when information is missing, an integration fails, or a person needs to step in.

  • We learn and ship faster. You turn ambiguous problems into focused releases, learn from real usage, and use that evidence to decide what to improve next.

What you will do

  • Examples of what you could build:

    • Trading: Help users go from an investment idea to a reviewed trade, with clear approvals, execution status, and visibility into what happened.

    • Strategies: Build ways to discover financial ideas, understand their upside and tradeoffs, explore how they fit a household's situation, and turn a saved strategy into a plan of action.

    • Tax filing: Bring document collection, missing-information requests, CPA review, and filing progress into one clear experience for households and their tax team.

    Across these features, you'll:

    • Own problems from discovery to launch. Talk with customers and financial experts, identify what matters, and decide what to build first.

    • Design the experience. Sketch, prototype, and refine interfaces with our designer. Make complex decisions and workflows feel clear.

    • Build across the stack. Ship interfaces, backend services, integrations, and AI workflows. Follow the problem wherever the implementation takes you.

    • Turn agents into useful products. Build ways for people to understand, review, and approve an agent's work, including workflows that span external tools and websites.

    • Make the whole flow work. Handle incomplete information, interruptions, retries, and human handoffs. Verify that the task actually finished correctly.

    • Use AI tools to ship and iterate. Move quickly, understand and check what you ship, and keep improving it through customer feedback and usage.

What we look for

  • Role-agnostic

    • Opportunity alignment: You want to help households manage complex finances and bring expert tax and financial planning to more people. You're excited to shape a product on a small, early team.

    • High agency: You see what needs doing and take responsibility for it. You can start with an incomplete brief, find the missing information, and make progress.

    • Exceptional collaboration: You make the people around you better: engineers, designers, CPAs, and Financial Planners. You seek feedback, say what you think, and follow through.

    • First-principles thinking: You start with the customer's problem, question assumptions, and can explain why your approach makes sense. You change your mind when the evidence changes.

  • Role-specific

    • Strong engineering fundamentals. You've built and shipped working software, can reason through unfamiliar systems, and care about correctness and maintainability.

    • Product judgment. You can turn an open-ended problem into a useful first release, explain what you left out, and define how you'll know it helped.

    • Design taste. You notice confusing interactions, care about the details, and can explain how your changes improve the experience.

    • You ship your own work. You're comfortable moving between the interface and backend, using AI coding tools thoughtfully, and verifying the result.

    • Bonus: startup, agent, or integration experience. You've built directly with users, worked with browser automation or AI agents, or connected systems that don't fit neatly together.

Prior experience with finance, AI or ML products, or our exact tech stack isn't required. Neither is a particular degree or school. We're interested in what you've built and how you think.

The starting salary for this position is between $140,250 - $207,775 USD. Candidate's location does not impact the posted salary range. The actual compensation offered will be based on a variety of job-related factors including relevant skills, education, and experience. This position also includes equity in CoinTracker and benefits like medical, dental, vision, 401(k), life insurance, and PTO.

Founded to transform retail finance, Ajaib Group is an Indonesian fintech unicorn breaking barriers to financial access. Having recently secured a $270M Series C—the single largest funding round in Southeast Asia over the past four years—we are backed by premier global investors including Y Combinator, Ribbit Capital, SoftBank, and SBI Holdings.  

To build world-class products, we assemble world-class talent. Supported by our fully remote work arrangement, our team spans Eastern Europe, the Middle East, India, and Southeast Asia, allowing you to work with brilliant engineers and builders from around the globe from wherever you are. We operate with an impact-driven purpose where everyone is the owner of our customers' satisfaction. Driven by a growth mindset and a fierce will to win, we refuse to settle and constantly push engineering boundaries.

Role Overview

As a Senior Web Engineer II in the Platform team, you build the web foundations that every Ajaib product team builds on: the design system and component library, shared packages, sign-in and session handling in the browser, and the build and release tooling. You own these foundations from design to production, treat other engineers as your customers, and help the engineers around you do better work.

  • Design, build and maintain shared web foundations: component library, design system, shared packages and the application shell.
  • Own features end to end: technical design, implementation, testing, release and support for the teams that use them.
  • Keep shared packages stable: clear APIs, semantic versioning, changelogs, migration guides and safe deprecation.
  • Build accessible, themeable, well-documented components that product teams can adopt without custom work.
  • Build and improve secure sign-in, session and token handling on the web, working with backend and Security teams.
  • Improve build speed, CI/CD pipelines, monorepo tooling and release automation for all web teams.
  • Set and measure performance budgets and quality standards, such as Core Web Vitals, bundle size and accessibility checks.
  • Write maintainable, well-tested code and give thoughtful code reviews.
  • Investigate production issues from error monitoring and feedback from product teams, and ship lasting fixes.
  • Mentor mid-level engineers and share good web practices across teams.
  • Own the integration of our centralized identity platform (OAuth2/OIDC) into all web properties, ensuring zero-trust session management and protecting against modern web vulnerabilities.
  • Establish and enforce company-wide frontend instrumentation standards. Build the core telemetry packages (logging, tracing, error boundaries) that product teams use to monitor their apps in production.
  • Education: Bachelor's degree in Computer Science or equivalent practical experience.
  • Experience: 5+ years of professional web engineering, including building shared libraries, design systems or tooling used by several teams.
  • Languages & Frameworks: Strong in TypeScript and JavaScript; deep experience with React and a modern framework such as Next.js (deep knowledge in App Router / Pages Router is a must); strong component design.
  • Architecture & Tooling: Experience with monorepos, bundlers, package publishing and build performance. 
  • Quality: Solid experience with unit, integration, visual and end-to-end testing, CI/CD and error monitoring.
  • Performance & Security: Strong in browser performance profiling, accessibility and web security, including authentication on the web. Deep understanding of browser mechanics, HTTP headers (CSP, CORS), cookie security policies, and token lifecycles.
  • Mindset: Ownership mindset, clear communication and a service attitude toward internal users. Experience in fintech or another regulated, high-traffic consumer product is a plus.

descriptions.job-19c9eiv:
BitGo (NYSE: BTGO) is the digital asset infrastructure company delivering custody, wallets, staking, trading, financing, stablecoins, and settlement services from regulated cold storage. Since 2013, BitGo has focused on accelerating the transition of the financial system to a digital asset economy. BitGo maintains a global presence and multiple regulated entities, including BitGo Bank & Trust, National Association, the first federally chartered digital asset trust bank owned by a publicly traded company. Today, BitGo serves thousands of institutions, including many of the industry's top brands, financial institutions, exchanges, and platforms, and millions of investors worldwide. For more information, visit www.bitgo.com.

This role will require being full-time onsite at our Toronto office to support collaborative team dynamics and innovative problem-solving.

BitGo is looking for a design leader who still designs. You will manage and mentor the design team, own the design system, and sit next to the Chief Product Officer on business strategy.

This is a player-coach role, and we mean it literally. You will carry your own design surfaces and ship them, alongside leading the team. Expect roughly 50% hands-on IC work to start, decreasing as the team scales. It will not go to zero — the person setting the craft bar should be practicing at it.

We are not a design-forward company today. We intend to become one, and we want you to lead that shift.

The team you will lead

The design team is small, senior, and self-sufficient. Each designer owns a wide vertical outright — trading, staking, DeFi vaults, earn, wallets, financing — with deep product context and strong opinions about the work. They are running at capacity, which is part of why this role carries real IC load: you will pick up the retail mobile experience and design system rather than distributing that work across a team that is already full.

What they have asked for is specific, and we are hiring against it: a leader who gets into the work early with product and engineering rather than arriving at the end, who can critique craft because they still practice it, who tells them plainly what the next level requires, and who gives the team air cover so they can do the deep work instead of patching to hit dates.

What you will own

  • Your own design work. You will own surfaces directly and ship them at the quality bar you are asking of everyone else. Discovery through spec, in Figma, in the reviews, on the hard problems.
  • The team's growth. Invest in each designer individually. Be explicit about what the next level requires and give people the work that gets them there. Feedback should be candid, specific, and about the craft. Respect the ownership designers already have — autonomy is how this team works best, and your job is to raise the ceiling, not take the pen.
  • Design's standing in the company. Amplify the team's visibility, voice, and strategic impact. Represent design in strategy, roadmap, and architecture conversations, and push for the client experience when nobody else in the room will.
  • Upstream involvement. Join product and engineering at discovery, not at handoff. Shape long-term roadmaps with PMs so the team builds toward a direction instead of absorbing late changes.
  • The design system. Own the system and component library end to end: tokens, patterns, governance, contribution model, and adoption across product teams. Translate company strategy into a system flexible enough that teams ship scalable experiences rather than one-off patches.
  • Systems design. Our platform spans seven product areas with shared primitives — accounts, wallets, assets, entitlements, approvals. Design the system, not the screen.
  • The discipline. Establish UX and systems thinking as a practice the whole organization runs on, not a stage a design team owns. Product managers, engineers, and business leads should be able to frame a client problem, map the system it lives in, and evaluate a solution against real client needs. That is how we ship value to every client type we serve, in every market we operate in — rather than a set of features that work for the loudest account.
  • How we work. Establish the processes a small team needs to move fast without losing quality: critique, documentation, design review, and clean handoffs with engineering. Set the quality bar and hold it, including for AI-assisted work.
  • Technical depth. Read a technical design, understand the constraint, and decide with engineering where to compromise, where to hold, and where a broader change is worth the cost. Get into the mechanics with the team on the hard edge cases — the crypto ones and the design ones.
  • The face of design. Be present and known internally, and represent BitGo design externally with clients, partners, and candidates.

What success looks like

By six months: the design system has a clear owner, a versioned component library, and measurable adoption. Product teams stop reinventing patterns. You have shipped design work of your own that the team points to as the standard. Every designer knows what their next level requires and has work that supports getting there.

By 12 months: design is in the room early on strategy, not late on execution. Product and engineering partners frame problems in client terms without being asked. The team has grown in size and capability. At least one flagship surface has shipped with a coherent, systemized experience clients notice.

Who you are

  • Experience leading design in financial services. Digital assets, or another domain of genuinely complex technical flows, strongly preferred.
  • You have built and owned a design system at scale, not just used one.
  • Hands-on in Figma and a role model for craft. You are shipping design work today, not describing work you shipped four years ago. You can sit in a critique and give feedback that is specific enough to act on.
  • Deep in UX. Strong product thinking, logical reasoning, and decisions grounded in data rather than taste alone.
  • You have managed designers and made them better. You care about how the team is doing, not only what it ships.
  • Technically literate. Comfortable with APIs, data models, and engineering trade-offs.
  • Direct communicator. You can hold a position with a Chief Product Officer, an engineering lead, or a client, and change your mind when the argument is better.
  • You want the mandate. Turning a technical, compliance-heavy platform into a design-led one is the appeal, not the obstacle.

Helpful, not required

  • Regulated environments: broker-dealer, trust company, bank, or qualified custodian.
  • Experience with complex permissioning, approval workflows, or multi-entity account structures.
  • Design leadership at a company that went through the same shift you would lead here.

Why Join BitGo?

Disrupting an industry takes vision, innovation, passion, technical chops, drive to deliver, collaboration, and execution. Join a team of great people who strive for excellence and personify our corporate values of ownership, craftsmanship, and open communication. We are looking for new colleagues who bring innovative ways of thinking and problem-solving, and who want risks to be part of the team that changes the world’s financial markets.

Benefits may vary based on location.

Pay Transparency Notice:

Depending upon your leveling and location, the compensation for this role averages between $210,000 and $250,000 CAD base salary. Equity, an annual performance bonus and an Ontario-based benefits package are also part of this role’s compensation.

Cryptocurrencies are the most disruptive change the financial services industry has seen in years. Join us and you'll be able to look back and say you were part of the team that transformed investing.

Working hand-in-hand with Product, Design, Sales, and Open Source Engineering, the team owns messaging, go-to-market strategy, content, and events that position OpenZeppelin as the security standard for onchain finance.

What you'll be doing

As OpenZeppelin’s Lead Product Marketer for Financial Services, you will own how we position, launch, and sell our solutions to banks, asset managers, and financial market infrastructures. You will lead the go-to-market for new institutional solutions, from positioning through launch and adoption, and make sure Sales has what it needs to win. You will work AI-native by default: building the workflows, agents, and tools that let you research faster, create better content, and give Sales assets that adapt to every account instead of going stale.

You will

  • Own positioning and messaging for our institutional solutions, defining value propositions, differentiators, and messaging by use case and buyer persona.
  • Lead product launches for new institutional solutions, from launch plans and timelines through announcement, assets, and post-launch adoption.
  • Enable Sales with AI-native assets: sales kits, pitch narratives, one-pagers, battlecards, and evaluation materials built to be customized per account and kept current, not static decks.
  • Run AI-powered competitive and market intelligenceby building workflows that track competitors, regulatory developments, and industry news, and turn them into actionable insights for Sales, Product, and leadership.
  • Build use-case and solution pages  directly in our CMS, explaining clearly what we offer, who it is for, and why it matters.
  • Support early adopter and design partner programs,  shaping the materials and narrative that turn institutional interest into qualified opportunities.
  • Contribute to institutional content, including research reports, thought leadership, and newsletter topics, using AI workflows to research, draft, and repurpose efficiently.
  • Create light social media content when valuable content or launches go live, in coordination with the wider Marketing team.
  • Close the loop with the product owners by bringing customer and market feedback into roadmap and packaging discussions.
  • Measure what matters by defining launch and adoption metrics and reporting on results.

Location

  • All positions at OpenZeppelin are 100% remote, however you should be located between UTC-5 and UTC+2 to be seriously considered for this position.

You have

  • 3+ years in product marketing at companies selling to institutions: financial services, digital asset service providers, or blockchain companies with an institutional customer base.
  • A proven track record of marketing to banks, asset managers, or market infrastructures at a company that actually won their business. You already know what these buyers want, how they evaluate, and what makes them move.
  • An AI-native way of working. You build and use AI workflows daily for content creation, research, competitive monitoring, and sales assets, and can show examples of what you’ve built.
  • A solid understanding of digital asset and tokenization use cases, such as tokenized deposits, money market funds, repo, and stablecoins.
  • Exceptional writing skills, with the ability to make complex technical and regulatory topics clear and credible for senior audiences.
  • Experience working closely with Sales and Product to turn strategy into assets that are actually used in deals.
  • Strong project management skills and comfort working through compliance and approval processes.
  • A self-driven, collaborative mindset that thrives in dynamic environments.

Nice to have

  • Experience in product marketing for services (security, consulting, or professional services), not only software products.
  • Experience building web pages through a headless CMS such as Sanity.
  • Familiarity with blockchain technology and smart contract development.
  • Experience running beta, pilot, or design partner programs.
  • Experience with HubSpot or similar marketing automation tools.

Logistics:

Our interview process takes place on Zoom and tends to consist of the following stages:

  • Recruiter Interview (30-45 min)
  • Hiring Manager Interview (60 min)
  • Team Interview (45 min)
  • Leadership Interview (30 min)
  • Paid, take-home work test (Lasting up to 10 days)
  • Reference checks

Please let us know if you require any accommodations for the interview process, and we’ll do our best to provide assistance.

Benefits

  • Meet your teammates at company gatherings around the world 😎
  • Enjoy the flexibility of fully remote work 🌎
  • Take the time you need with flexible time off 🏝
  • Grow your family with 8 weeks of paid leave for primary caregivers, 4 weeks for secondary caregivers, and a one-time $3,600 baby bonus 💙
  • Build your ideal home office with up to $500 in equipment support 🪑
  • Stay covered with medical insurance 🏥
  • Keep growing with learning and development opportunities 🧠
  • Get a monthly stipend for your preferred co-working space 💻

At OpenZeppelin, we are an equal opportunity employer and we value different perspectives. We are committed to building a diverse workforce. This includes but is not limited to gender, race, sexual orientation, religion, national origin and other characteristics that make each one of us unique. In this uniqueness, we find the most value. Come join us!

Use of AI as part of the recruiting process

As part of OpenZeppelin’s recruitment process, we may use automated tools, including artificial intelligence, to assist in reviewing applications and assessing candidate qualifications. These tools are used to support our People team by identifying relevant skills and experience, and are not used to make decisions solely by automated means. All hiring decisions involve human review. Any personal data provided as part of your application will be processed in accordance with OpenZeppelin’s Data Privacy Notice.

If you have questions about this recruitment process or would like to request human review of your application, please contact us at talent@openzeppelin.com.

About Aspora

People on the move deserve a bank that moves with them. Since 2022, Aspora has been building a borderless financial operating system that makes money as mobile and transparent as its users.

Backed by influential venture capitalists like Sequoia Capital, Greylock Partners, Hummingbird Ventures, Y Combinator & Global Founders Capital. We're a team of 150+ across India, the UK, the UAE, EU and the US, working with extreme ownership, radical candour, and an obsession with customer impact.

We celebrate builders who question assumptions, ship fast, and turn regulatory complexity into elegant solutions. If you’re driven to redefine what global banking can be, we’d love to build the future with you.

About the Role

This role exists to be the trusted financial partner that NRI customers actually need. Not a support agent. Not a script-reader. A person who understands the full complexity of their financial life across borders.

NRI banking is not simple. FEMA compliance, cross-border tax implications, NRO vs NRE decisions: customers get these wrong when no one takes the time to explain them. You will. You'll build real relationships, diagnose real problems, and feed what you learn back into how the product evolves.

You'll sit at the intersection of customer experience and product thinking. What you hear every day shapes what we build next.

What You'll Do

  • Own the end-to-end customer relationship for a book of NRI customers: from onboarding through ongoing advisory and retention

  • Drive adoption of NRI banking products by translating regulatory complexity (FEMA, tax implications, account structures) into plain, confident guidance

  • Resolve account, KYC, transaction, and documentation issues independently: first contact to confirmed resolution, no handoffs

  • Identify recurring friction patterns across your customer interactions and translate them into specific product and process improvement recommendations

  • Build and maintain detailed CRM records and contribute to internal playbooks that make the whole team sharper

What We're Looking For

  • Experience in a customer-facing role in banking, fintech, financial services, or high-touch customer success

  • Strong understanding of financial products; ability to explain them simply — NRI banking knowledge is a plus, curiosity is a requirement

  • High ownership mindset: you treat a customer's problem as yours until it is solved

  • Ability to operate without a script — you diagnose, improvise, and escalate with full context when needed

  • Comfortable with regulatory and compliance complexity; you don't shy away from hard conversations

  • Clear written and verbal communication in English; able to hold nuanced conversations about money with customers under stress

Nice to Have

  • Additional Indian languages (Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, or others)

  • Experience in a startup or early-stage environment

Why Join Aspora

  • You'll be the primary relationship owner for NRI customers navigating one of the most under-served financial journeys in global banking — your work directly shapes their trust in Aspora

  • You'll move fast on real problems: no ticket queues that disappear into the void. You own resolution.

  • What you learn from customers will directly feed product decisions. Your feedback loop to the team is short and real.

  • You'll develop rare expertise: cross-border financial regulation, NRI banking structures, and the nuance of serving a globally mobile customer base

  • Competitive salary, comprehensive benefits, and ESOPs aligned with Aspora's long-term vision.

What Success Looks Like

  • Customers feel genuinely guided through their NRI banking setup — not just processed

  • Issue resolution is end-to-end owned, with measurable reduction in repeat contacts

  • Customer insights are regularly surfaced to the product and ops teams in actionable form

  • CRM records and internal playbooks are detailed, current, and used by the wider team

About HIFI

HIFI is a stablecoin infrastructure company building technology for the next-generation of financial products. We build tools for payments and tokenized money products across money movement, cards, and capital markets. Institutions and enterprises already use our platform and APIs to move billions of dollars in production environments around the world, and we are still early.

 

Founded in 2022, our organization is flat and our team is talent dense. We work in person at our office in Flatiron and are intentional about who we work with. We've raised $37 million from world-class investors, including a Series A led by Left Lane Capital.

 

About the Team

HIFI's Go-To-Market team brings our infrastructure to the companies and institutions building on stablecoins. The team spans sales, partnerships, solutions engineering, and customer success. We work as one unit across the full customer lifecycle, from the first conversation through integration, launch, and scaled volume.

 

We're growing our Go-To-Market team and hiring an Account Executive to drive new business across stablecoin settlement and payments. You'll own the full sales cycle for a portfolio of prospects and customers, from prospecting and discovery through negotiation, close, and handoff to implementation.

 

Responsibilities

  • Own the full sales cycle with institutional clients, including fintechs, payment companies, banks, and enterprises, from first conversation through signed contract.

  • Build and manage your own pipeline through outbound prospecting, inbound leads, referrals, and partner introductions.

  • Run discovery to understand how prospects move money today, and make the case for how HIFI's stablecoin settlement fits their payment flows.

  • Lead product demos and work with solutions engineering to scope integrations and answer technical questions.

  • Coordinate with compliance on client onboarding and due diligence so deals close without delays.

  • Negotiate pricing and commercial terms, and work with legal to get contracts signed.

  • Keep the CRM accurate and forecast your pipeline reliably each month and quarter.

  • Bring customer feedback to product and marketing, and help shape positioning, pricing, and the roadmap based on what you hear in the market.

 

You might be a fit if

  • 4+ years of closing experience as an account executive, ideally selling infrastructure or API products to fintechs, payment companies, banks, or crypto companies.

  • A track record of meeting or exceeding quota on complex, multi-stakeholder deals with long sales cycles.

  • You understand how money moves, including wires, ACH, cross-border payments, and treasury operations, and can explain where stablecoin settlement fits.

  • Experience selling to technical buyers and working alongside engineers to scope integrations.

  • You've built your own pipeline through outbound and don't rely only on inbound leads.

  • Comfortable negotiating pricing and contract terms, and working through diligence and compliance reviews with institutional buyers.

  • You keep your pipeline organized and forecast accurately.

  • You enjoy early-stage selling, where you shape the pitch, the process, and the playbook as you go.

  • Comfort operating in a fast-moving environment where products, regulation, and the market evolve quickly.

 

Why This Role Matters

Most of the institutions HIFI works with are still deciding how stablecoins fit into the way they move money. In this role, you'll help them make that decision and get them live on HIFI's rails. You'll shape how HIFI brings on new partners, and the partners you bring on will help define the company's growth.

 

Additional Requirement

Must be within a commutable distance from our office and able to work in person most days of the week.

 

Equal Opportunity Statement

HIFI is an equal opportunity employer. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other legally protected status. We also provide reasonable accommodations during the hiring process.

Featured benefits

Medical insurance, Vision insurance, Dental insurance

About Fasset

At Fasset, we believe your money should answer to you. We are a banking and investment platform built around a simple idea: more people should have access to the financial system, regardless of where they live. We are building the global financial system for ownership, one that moves what you earn into what you own, so that what you can own is never decided by where you were born.

We operate across emerging markets, with a particular focus on the Middle East, Asia and Africa. Founded by Mohammad Raafi Hossain and Daniel Ahmed, Fasset has become a company valued at $1 billion and holds regulatory approvals across markets including the UAE, Indonesia, Malaysia, the EU, Türkiye and Pakistan.

We are a fast-moving, global team scaling a regulated platform across multiple markets. Our culture runs on HEART: Humble Curiosity, Enthusiasm, Act Like Owners, Raise the Bar, and Tenacity. And we hold one simple view about the people who join us: the owners arrive early.

About the role

You keep Fasset's front door safe and open. You make the judgment calls on onboarding, screening and monitoring cases, and you run the tools that do the first pass, so they get sharper every month. You'll work across several regulated markets, alongside our Compliance team and Customer Experience.

What you'll do

  • Review onboarding cases that need human judgment, and decide or escalate with a written rationale
  • Clear sanctions and PEP screening alerts, and work ongoing monitoring alerts through to closure
  • Configure and tune our KYC, screening and monitoring tools, including their AI-assisted features, to cut false positives without missing real risk
  • Work with technology partners on false positives, document disputes and tool issues
  • Write and maintain procedures, and train support analysts on verification basics
  • Spot patterns in rejections, fraud attempts and alerts, and take them to Compliance and Product with evidence
  • Keep case records complete and audit-ready
  • Review complaints escalated by support analysts, find the root cause, and resolve them or route them to the right team
  • Keep the analyst who owns the case informed, so the customer gets one clear, consistent answer
  • Review appeals on cases first decided by a support analyst, together with our Compliance team
  • Handle cases involving frozen accounts or blocked transactions in line with our sanctions policy
  • Put security issues, suspected scams and possible loss of funds ahead of everything else
  • Treat every customer fairly and consistently, with extra care for customers who may be vulnerable

What you'll bring

Must have

  • 4 or more years in compliance operations, KYC/AML or financial crime at a bank, fintech, payments company or virtual asset service provider (VASP)
  • Strong judgment on document fraud, customer due diligence and enhanced due diligence
  • Hands-on experience with sanctions and PEP screening and ongoing monitoring
  • Experience configuring or tuning screening or monitoring rules in a compliance platform
  • Clear written English, including procedures and case notes others can follow
  • The ability to work independently across time zones

Nice to have

  • Excellent spoken English, clear and confident on the phone
  • Experience handling formal complaints in a regulated financial services business
  • Crypto or virtual asset compliance experience
  • Knowledge of requirements from the Securities Commission Malaysia, VARA, OJK or the Central Bank of Bahrain
  • A recognized AML certification, such as CAMS or ICA
  • Japanese, Korean, Arabic, Indonesian, Malay, or Spanish

Not a 100% match? We'd still love to hear from you. We hire for potential and HEART, not a checklist, so apply if the mission excites you.

What we offer

  • Ownership from day one. High-trust, high-ownership culture where you get room to act like an owner and the support to raise the bar.
  • Competitive package, benchmarked across our markets and reviewed as you grow.
  • A real path forward through Grow with Fasset (#GwF), our L1–L7 progression framework with both IC and Manager tracks.
  • Global exposure working alongside a team spread across seven markets, solving problems that matter for emerging economies.
  • Learning and development support to keep growing your craft.
